title: How Plants Eat
summary: This lesson explores photosynthesis, the process by which plants make food using sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water. Students will learn how chlorophyll, stomata, roots, and the Calvin cycle work together to produce glucose and release oxygen.

sections.text: Scene: A green leaf is shown under bright sunlight with a close-up diagram of chlorophyll capturing the light energy. I wonder...?: How do plants make food? Answer: Photosynthesis is how plants make food, with chlorophyll in leaves capturing sunlight.

Scene: An illustration shows carbon dioxide entering through stomata on the leaf and water being absorbed through the roots in the soil. I wonder...?: What do plants take in from their environment? Answer: Plants take in carbon dioxide through stomata and water through roots.

Scene: A visual diagram traces light energy converting into chemical energy as glucose is produced and oxygen is released. I wonder...?: What is produced during this process? Answer: They produce glucose and release oxygen, while the Calvin cycle converts light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar.

learning_objectives: Understand how plants make food through photosynthesis
Identify how plants take in carbon dioxide and water
Explain the role of the Calvin cycle in energy conversion
